question.prompt: While Steve and LeRoy are fishing \(1\) mile from shore, their boat springs a leak, and water comes in at a constant rate of \(10\) gallons per minute. The boat will sink if it takes in more than \(30\) gallons of water. Steve starts rowing toward the shore at a constant rate of \(4\) miles per hour while LeRoy bails water out of the boat. What is the slowest rate, in gallons per minute, at which LeRoy can bail if they are to reach the shore without sinking?

solutions.explanation:
First find how long they must keep the boat afloat. At \(4\) miles per hour, traveling \(1\) mile takes
\[
\frac14\text{ hour}=15\text{ minutes}.
\]
During those \(15\) minutes, the leak brings in \(10\cdot15=150\) gallons. Since at most \(30\) gallons may remain in the boat, LeRoy must remove at least
\[
150-30=120\text{ gallons}.
\]
His constant bailing rate must therefore be at least
\[
\frac{120}{15}=8\text{ gallons per minute}.
\]
This rate works throughout the trip: water accumulates at \(10-8=2\) gallons per minute, increasing from \(0\) to exactly \(30\) gallons on arrival. Exactly \(30\) gallons is allowed because the boat sinks only if the amount exceeds \(30\). Any slower rate leaves too much water by the end of the trip. Thus the slowest rate is \(\boxed{8}\) gallons per minute, choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
solutions.title: Budget the water for the trip
